transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Ever since they changed my position at the shop, I just can’t seem to adjust, and it’s throwing off my work and my whole routine. I'm just having a really hard time coping with the new setup.
When did this change in your position happen, and how long after that did you start feeling unable to cope? Have these difficulties lasted most days since then?

The position change happened about a month ago, and within a week or two of the switch, I started feeling this constant dread and defeat. It has been going on almost every single day since then, and I just can't seem to shake it.

Was this position change something most people would see as a major stressful event, like a demotion or serious conflict, or does your reaction feel much stronger than the change itself would usually cause? Have these feelings significantly affected your work, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

The change is frustrating, but my reaction feels way out of proportion—I'm constantly on the verge of tears, snapping at people, and just feeling completely defeated. It has definitely taken a toll, as my new supervisor already warned me about slipping numbers and missed deadlines, and I've been backing out of plans with friends and falling behind on my art commissions.

Around the time this started, was there any other major stressor or trauma—like a death, breakup, assault, or accident—or does it seem clearly tied only to the job change? Have you ever had similar symptoms before this event?

No, there hasn't been any other trauma or loss—this is completely tied to the sudden restructuring and shift change at the shop. I’ve never experienced anything like this before, as I've always been able to handle my work and routines without any issues.

Since this started, have there been stretches of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly all day, even outside of work stress? Or do the feelings mainly flare when you’re dealing with the job change and its consequences?

These feelings are definitely tied directly to the job change and its aftermath, rather than being some independent depression. The dread and loss of interest in my sculpting and socializing only started when the restructuring happened a month ago. I know if they just moved me back to my old team or eased the quotas, I would get right back to my normal, active self.

Have these symptoms started to ease at all when you’re away from work, or do they stay just as strong all the time? Also, if the job situation were resolved, do you think the symptoms would go away within a few months?

No, they don't ease up at home—I just go home feeling so wound up and defeated that I end up sitting on the couch staring at my half-finished sculptures. But if they moved me back to my old team or eased the quotas, I really believe I could get back to my normal routine within a few months.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began within 1–2 weeks of an identifiable psychosocial stressor (job restructuring/position change), occur nearly daily for about a month, are described as disproportionate to the stressor, and have caused clear occupational and social impairment. The patient denies other trauma and indicates the symptoms are tied to the stressor rather than an independent depressive episode, supporting an adjustment disorder diagnosis.
